question: Do the opt-in CUDA transfer modes (bit 1 lean prepare: reused page-locked host level 0, chunked copy overlapped with the uploads, no wait for the device pyramid, no host copy of levels 1..top when the fine search runs on the device; bit 2 lean calls: no timing events or memsets, fine requests read from mapped memory, completion polled in mapped memory instead of cudaStreamSynchronize) keep the CUDA backend's outputs bit-identical to the same build's CPU backend, and how do they change the per-frame time (prepare + match) of the 17 fixtures on the RTX PRO 4000 against transfer mode 0 of the same build?
core_unchanged: git diff 31820ad c1068b2 -- cpp-core/src cpp-core/include is empty, so no core identity run is needed this round
sources: git archive of c1068b2 (cpp-core without docs for the PC; cpp-core, macos-cli and Test Images for the Mac), unpacked into fresh directories

pc.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell, compute capability 12.0, 24 GB, PCIe 5.0 x16, driver 596.71, WDDM, no display attached
pc.toolchain: MSVC 19.44, CUDA 13.2 Update 2 (nvcc V13.2.86), CMake, Ninja, Release, CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120, nvcc -fmad=false -lineinfo, static cudart
pc.build: c1068b2 with FPM_BUILD_EXPERIMENTS=ON FPM_WITH_CUDA=ON; every timing and identity arm runs this one build's fpm_frame_bench
pc.affinity: drivers start with `start /affinity C03C02` (P-cores 1,10-13,22,23); children inherit it

mac: Apple M4 Pro: research build of c1068b2 (GUI, OpenCV, experiments; no CUDA) passes ctest, since coarse_ncc.cpp's frame prepare changed for every backend
inputs: the 17 compare_versions cases as 8-bit PGM (C:\r51\bundle\pgm), checked against the round-1 manifest (sha256 3a539fec058b4f42e613c074a8fcb0f697ae2ca671cd76645bc8a23b6cd8e64f) before any run

arms.m0: 2,1,256,0,0: CUDA, device pyramid, fine batch 256, fused coarse, transfer mode 0 (the merged backend's behaviour; the timing baseline)

identity_only.m3_cpu_pyramid: 2,0,256,0,3 (lean prepare does not apply; lean calls do)
identity_only.m1_cpu_fine: 2,1,0,0,1 (fine search on the CPU: lean prepare copies levels 1..top back and waits)

metric: per-frame time = fpm_frame_prepare + fpm_frame_match (image decoding and frame/pattern creation excluded); steady = median of 5 calls after 500 ms of untimed calls in the same process; cold = that process's first call. In lean modes prepare returns before the device pyramid is built, so only prepare + match is compared, never prepare alone. Lean calls report device_ms -1; device times come from the separate Nsight runs.

gates.ctest: the PC c1068b2 build passes ctest with experimental_cuda_backend and experimental_cuda_kernels run (not skipped); the Mac c1068b2 research build passes ctest
gates.identity: every run of every arm (timing rounds and identity-only runs) returns matches bit-identical to the cpu arm of the same round, case and mode; zero mismatches and zero failed runs
gates.mutants: cuda_mutants.py on c1068b2: T1-T10 (transfer modes) all KILLED; the 24 earlier mutants give the 7f5737b outcome again (22 KILLED, N2 and F2 SURVIVED, argued equivalent in CUDA_BACKEND_zh-TW.md); the unmutated and restored trees pass. U1-U4 (a missing system fence, a missing wait for the previous upload, counters not zeroed on allocation) are reported, not gated: a race or fresh-allocation contents the tests need not observe

hypotheses.H1: steady geometric mean of m3/m0 over the 17 cases is below 0.6 in each mode (exhaustive, fast, subpixel); pilot 0.42/0.41/0.48
hypotheses.H2: at least 16 of the 17 cases are faster with m3 than m0 in each mode; pilot 17/17, closest Src4 fast (0.93)
hypotheses.H3: m3 is faster than cpu on all 17 cases in each mode; pilot closest Src9 fast (0.26 vs 0.29 ms), the case where m0 was slower than cpu
hypotheses.descriptive: m1 and m2 (each change alone), cold first-call times, process peak RSS and retained device bytes are reported, not gated

timing.tool: benchmark_frame_backend.py --rounds 8 --repeat 5 --warmup-ms 500, arms cpu, m0, m1, m2, m3 (round 0 kept but left out of the summary; arm order alternates by round; fresh process per run)
timing.identity_only_run: benchmark_frame_backend.py --rounds 2 --repeat 1 --warmup-ms 0 with arms cpu and the five identity-only arms
timing.summary: frame_backend_summary.py --reference m0 --arm m1 --arm m2 --arm m3 --h1 0.6 --h2 16 for H1/H2, and --reference cpu --arm m3 for H3 (all 17 faster)
timing.quiet: nothing else runs on the PC during the timing run; mutants and profiling run afterwards
timing.no_drops: no run is dropped or repeated; a failed run is reported as failed

decision_rule: The transfer modes are kept as opt-in research options when every gate passes. H1-H3 are reported as measured; a failure is disclosed, not tuned away. Defaults (transfer mode 0, core and GUI) do not change.
not_formal: pilot/xfer_pilot.cu (transfer and wait latencies), pilot1 (two rounds of the five arms on the development tree, 0 mismatches) and the mutant pilot (the original T7, `same = !levels.empty()`, survived: it is equivalent when the level count shrinks and undefined behaviour when it grows, so it was replaced before this registration by the height-change mutant and a test step that changes only the height) chose the design and the thresholds and are archived as selection evidence only
profiling: Nsight Systems (--trace=cuda,nvtx,wddm) of m0 and m3 on Src7, Src9, Src5-0 exhaustive and Src6 subpixel, plus short traces of Src7, after the formal runs; their times are not formal
